newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CENTERTEL SEES 200,000 PHONES BY YR-END.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CENTERTEL SEES 200,000 PHONES BY YR-END.

text.p: Poland's cellular telephone operator Centertel SA expects the number of its clients to rise to more than 200,000 in 1997 from the current 160,000, the firm's director general said on Tuesday.
Marek Jozefiak told an international conference of cellular phone companies operating in the NMT analogue system that Centertel gained 70,000 new subscribers in 1996.

"By the end of this year we expect to service more than 200,000 subscribers. The monthly dynamics of sales is between 7,000 and 8,000 phones," Jozefiak said. He added, however, the monthly growth was unlikely to keep up throughout the year.
Jozefiak said there were no particular limits on the number of new subscribers Centertel was able to accomodate.

He said the company was ready to erect more than a dozen thousand of cellular phone booths activated by microchip cards in areas of low saturation with telephones, if the need for such a project arose.

On Monday the country's telecommunications monopolist TPSA said the number of telephones per 100 people grew to 17 in mid- February from less than 16 at the start of 1996. However, phone saturation in rural areas was only 6.8 per 100 people.
Jozefiak said that by November Centertel would sign agreements with operators in Sweden, Norway and Ukraine for its subscribers to be able to use their phones in these countries.
